items.stem: In a RAG pipeline, why does chunk size matter for answer quality?

options.text: Chunks that are too large dilute relevance; too small lose context
options.rationale: Correct: chunk size trades off focused relevance against enough surrounding context.

options.text: Chunk size sets the model's training data
options.rationale: Chunking affects retrieval, not model training.
Over-large chunks bring in irrelevant text and hurt retrieval.

options.text: Chunk size determines the S3 storage class
options.rationale: Storage class is unrelated to chunking.

items.explanation: Correct: chunk size trades off focused relevance against enough surrounding context.

items.stem: To keep answers trustworthy, the generation step should:

options.text: Ground answers in retrieved context and cite sources, refusing when context is missing
options.rationale: Correct: grounding and citation with graceful refusal keeps answers verifiable.

options.text: Answer from the model's general knowledge for speed
options.rationale: Ungrounded answers defeat the purpose of RAG and can hallucinate.

options.text: Never include citations to save tokens
options.rationale: Citations are what make the answer verifiable.

options.text: Always fabricate a source if none is found
options.rationale: Fabricating sources is a serious integrity failure.

items.explanation: Correct: grounding and citation with graceful refusal keeps answers verifiable.

items.stem: Which TWO improve retrieval quality in a document-intelligence pipeline? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: hybrid search improves recall across exact and semantic matches.

options.text: Use the same embedding model for indexing and querying
options.rationale: Correct: consistent embeddings keep vector distances meaningful.

options.text: Mix embeddings from different models in one index

options.rationale: Metadata often helps filtering and ranking.

items.explanation: Correct: hybrid search and a consistent embedding model both improve retrieval quality.
